ai.literal: Enmity, they say, to all lives, division called, lack of goodness, producing disease.
ai.translation: They say that enmity is the disease that breeds the evil called division among all living beings.
ai.modern: எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் பிரிவினை என்னும் தீமையை உண்டாக்கும் நோயே இகல் என்று அறிஞர் கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: The couplet defines enmity (இகல்) as a destructive disease (நோய்). It affects all living beings by creating a lack of harmony or goodness (பண்பின்மை), which manifests as division and separation (பகல்). By calling it a disease, the poet emphasizes that enmity is an unnatural affliction that destroys the natural unity of life.

ai.literal: Division intending, unloving things even if done, hostility intending, harmful things not doing is best.
ai.translation: Even if others commit unloving acts with the intent to cause division, it is best not to do them harm with the intent of hostility.
ai.modern: மற்றவர்கள் நம்மைப் பிரிக்க எண்ணி அன்பற்ற செயல்களைச் செய்தாலும், நாம் அவர்கள் மேல் பகை கொண்டு துன்பம் தரும் செயல்களைச் செய்யாமல் இருப்பதே சிறந்ததாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet advises against retaliating to divisive and unloving acts. The word pakal refers to division or separation, while paṟṟā denotes actions lacking attachment or affection. Even when subjected to such deliberate attempts to divide, the best course of action is to refrain from doing harm out of hostility. True greatness lies in breaking the cycle of enmity rather than returning harm for harm.

ai.literal: Hostility called grievous disease if removed, failing without, decay without glory it will give.
ai.translation: If one removes the grievous disease called hostility, it will yield unfailing and undecaying glory.
ai.modern: இகல் என்று சொல்லப்படும் துன்பம் தரும் நோயை ஒருவன் தன் மனதிலிருந்து நீக்கிவிட்டால், அது அவனுக்கு அழிவில்லாத நிலையான புகழைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes hostility as a grievous disease that afflicts the mind. The word 'இகல்' (hostility or enmity) is paired with 'எவ்வ நோய்' (grievous disease) to emphasize how destructive it is to one's own well-being. If a person can completely remove this disease, the very act of curing themselves of hatred will grant them 'விளக்கம்' (glory or brightness) that is both 'தவல் இல்லா' (unfailing) and 'தா இல்' (undecaying). Thus, letting go of enmity is presented not just as a moral good, but as the ultimate path to lasting greatness.

ai.literal: Among joys joy it will yield, hostility called among sorrows sorrow if destroyed.
ai.translation: If the greatest of sorrows called hostility is destroyed, it will yield the greatest of joys.
ai.modern: இகல் என்று சொல்லப்படும் மிகப்பெரிய துன்பம் ஒருவனை விட்டு ஒழிந்தால் அது அவனுக்கு எல்லா இன்பங்களிலும் சிறந்த இன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes hostility as the worst possible sorrow a person can experience. If one can completely eradicate this destructive feeling, the result is not merely peace, but the highest form of joy. The poet uses the contrasting phrases 'sorrow of sorrows' and 'joy of joys' to emphasize how deeply hostility affects human happiness.

ai.literal: Hostility before having-yielded to-behave those-who-are-able-(acc.) who-indeed to-conquer-will-attempt nature they?
ai.translation: Who would even attempt to conquer those who have the strength to yield in the face of hostility?
ai.modern: பகைமை எதிர்ப்படும்போது வளைந்து கொடுத்து நடக்கும் ஆற்றல் உடையவர்களை வெல்ல நினைக்கும் தன்மையுடையவர் எவரும் இலர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the strategic value of yielding. When faced with hostility (இகல்), choosing to step back or yield (சாய்ந்து) rather than retaliating is not a weakness, but a profound strength. The poet asks rhetorically who could possibly possess the nature to conquer those who are capable of such disciplined restraint. By yielding, one diffuses the enmity, making it impossible for opponents to achieve a victory over them.

ai.literal: In enmity excelling is sweet, he who says, life declining and perishing is near.
ai.translation: The life of a man who says it is sweet to excel in enmity is close to decline and ruin.
ai.modern: பகைமையில் வெற்றி பெறுவது இனிமையானது என்று சொல்லும் ஒருவனது வாழ்க்கை, விரைவில் குறைந்து அழிந்து போவதற்கு அருகில் உள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against finding pleasure in conflict and hostility. The phrase 'இகலின் மிகல் இனிது' captures the dangerous mindset of someone who enjoys overpowering others through enmity. The words 'தவலும்' (declining) and 'கெடலும்' (perishing) show the inevitable two-stage downfall of such a person. Ultimately, the poet states that ruin is 'நணித்து' (near) for anyone who makes a lifestyle out of hostility.

ai.literal: victory attaining true-reality they-will-not-see hostility desiring painful understanding-those-of
ai.translation: Those of painful understanding who desire hostility will not see the true reality of attaining victory.
ai.modern: பகைமையை விரும்புகின்ற துன்பமான அறிவை உடையவர்கள், வெற்றியை அடையும் உண்மையான பொருளைக் காண மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the desire for hostility with the attainment of true success. The phrase 'இகல் மேவல் இன்னா அறிவினவர்' describes people whose minds are afflicted by a painful or harmful desire to engage in enmity. Because their understanding is clouded by this destructive urge, they 'காணார்' (will not see) the 'மெய்ப்பொருள்' (true reality or substance) of 'மிகல் மேவல்' (attaining victory or greatness). The repetition of the word 'மேவல்' (desiring or attaining) highlights the choice between pursuing conflict and pursuing genuine success.

ai.literal: To hostility yielding before is prosperity; it conquering if one intends, will hasten indeed ruin.
ai.translation: Yielding to hostility brings prosperity. If one intends to conquer it by fighting back, ruin will hasten to them.
ai.modern: இகலுக்கு எதிர்த்து நிற்காமல் பணிந்து போவது நன்மையைத் தரும். அந்த இகலை வளர்த்து வெல்ல நினைத்தால், அது அழிவை விரைந்து கொண்டுவரும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the outcomes of yielding to enmity versus fueling it. The phrase 'எதிர்சாய்தல்' (yielding before) suggests stepping back from a conflict, which the poet says brings 'ஆக்கம்' (prosperity or growth). Conversely, 'மிகல் ஊக்கின்' means intending to increase or conquer through hostility. Doing so 'ஊக்கும் கேடு' (hastens ruin), with the word 'ஆம்' acting as an emphatic particle to stress the certainty of destruction.

ai.literal: Hostility he-will-not-see prosperity when-coming; it increasing he-will-see ruin to-bring-about.
ai.translation: When prosperity is on its way, a person will not entertain hostility; but to bring about his own ruin, he will seek to increase it.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுக்கு நல்வாழ்வு வரும் காலத்தில் அவன் பகைமையை விரும்ப மாட்டான்; அவனுக்கு அழிவு வரப்போகிறது என்றால் அந்தப் பகைமையை மேலும் வளர்த்துக்கொள்வான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet connects a person's inclination toward conflict with their impending fortune or downfall. The phrase 'ஆக்கம் வருங்கால்' (when prosperity comes) indicates that a mind destined for success naturally avoids enmity. Conversely, when ruin is imminent ('கேடு தரற்கு'), a person is drawn to escalate conflicts, actively seeking the increase of hostility. The poet illustrates that the choice to ignore or amplify discord is the very mechanism that brings about wealth or destruction.

ai.literal: From enmity will happen painful things all; from friendship will happen good benefit called wealth.
ai.translation: All painful evils arise from enmity. The great wealth of good grace arises from friendship.
ai.modern: பகைமையால் துன்பம் தரும் செயல்கள் எல்லாம் உண்டாகும். நட்பினால் நல்ல பயன் எனப்படும் பெருஞ்செல்வம் உண்டாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the outcomes of enmity and friendship. 'இகல்' (enmity) is identified as the source of all painful and harmful things. In contrast, 'நகல்' (friendship or rejoicing) brings about the great wealth ('செருக்கு') of good benefits ('நன்னயம்'). Here, 'செருக்கு', which often means pride, is used positively to mean abundance or greatness.
